title: Effect of rapid thermal annealing on the optoelectronic figures of merit of a vanadium nitride/porous silicon heterojunction photodetector
content: Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) is an essential step in the fabrication of photovoltaic devices. It considerably improves crystallinity, dopant activation, electrical conductivity, optical efficiency, and contact formation while minimizing unwanted diffusion. These improvements, in turn, facilitate the fabrication of high-performance devices. In this study, vanadium nitride (VN) thin films and porous silicon (PSi) were prepared using reactive DC sputtering and photoelectrochemical etching (PECE) techniques, respectively. The effects of RTA at 1023 K for 35 s on the structural, morphological, optical, and electrical properties of the VN films and the figures of merit properties of VN/PSi/n-Si heterojunction photodetectors were systematically studied. X-ray diffraction (XRD) studies confirmed that the crystallinity of the film improved after RTA. The optical energy gap decreased from 3.63 to 3.58 eV after RTA. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed that the RTA process increased the particle size of the VN film and enhanced grain integration on the porous silicon surface. The fabrication and characterization of the VN/PSi/n-Si heterojunction photodetector are demonstrated. The dark I–V characteristics demonstrated a significant improvement in junction quality, with the ideality factor decreasing from 1.64 to 1.19 and the barrier height increasing from 0.77 to 0.83 V. The annealed photodetector exhibited a photosensitivity of 2300% at −10 V. Its responsivity increased from 2.69 to 3.76 A W−1 at 560 nm after RTA. The improved performance of the VN/PSi/n-Si heterojunction (HJ) photodetector after RTA open new opportunities for many applications that require enhanced response to low-intensity light accompanied by a significantly high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), such as high-speed optical communication, environmental sensing and biosensing applications.
